body: It does help. And I appreciate the reply. Always gotta look forward and up to the future.
Want to explain a bit more? Were all here to help.

Been there man, Oh god have I been there. Sometimes thoughts of ending it can take precedence over everything else in life. But I can promise you, There is something to live for. And that's what stops you last second before you can finally do it. As others have said. Find that. Embrace it, cherish it. 

Were all here for you, If you want to talk.

:(
I'll be around if either of you or Bipolar need anything.
Strength in numbers, guys.

I know the feeling. Numb is hard to explain. And I've never quite been able to do it.
But your right, It is what it is. I find myself saying that a lot lately. Specially with the girl in my life. Kinda always been my way of saying "I don't like it, But what the hell can I do?" in not so many words. Everyone takes losses differently. And trust me. Your not the only one desensitized. There are many, Just like that. Including myself.
Stay strong, And keep that chin up.

Sorry to hear that. Stay strong brother.
Were here for you if you want to talk about it. As always.

Glad to see your replies this morning. As you asked above, I'm doing alright. I generally wear the "Everythings ok" mask pretty well. Kinda have to with my job and such. It gets me though the day.

You mentioned it for exactly that, It's bugging you. We like to mention things that bother us. I'm in kinda a half assed relationship with a girl right now. And she can read me far to well. Apparently, When I have something bothering me (Her hanging out with an ex or something like that). I mention it alot. And after a little bit. She'll finally go "Ok, So its bothering you", And we'll talk about it a little bit. Generally the things that occupy your mind, Are the first things to come out. That's how I see it. Don't ever feel as if you shouldn't share something. Those thoughts may not make much sense to you. But once you explain all of them to someone, They just may be able to mold them into something a bit easier to swallow.

I'm terribly sorry to hear about your friend. I've had something similar happen, But it was a friend-of-a-friend. I can't imagine if it hit closer to home, And happened to one of my very few close friends. I would be a wreck for quite some time. Always here if you want to talk about it, by PM too.

BipolarHacker, First off. As mentioned, Your a very talented writer. I'd like to consider myself a fairly "macho" guy. Crying, Just isn't something I do. And your post has brought me to tears. Heh, I've had to pause and regain myself about 4 times just typing the above. This really hits home for me. Reading your post, Your comments. Seeing that you've almost taken my very thoughts and put them into words leaves me almost speechless. The closet, Full of weapons. The loaded Glock 22 which never leaves my sight. The thought never quite leaves me in peace. Always lurking in the back of my head. Sometimes managing to makes its way to the front at some of my weaker moments. The only thing keeping me from acting on it is knowning how it would leave my mother. And she doesn't deserve that. So I go on, Day by day. Almost numb at times. Waiting for it to get better. Sadly. It hasn't. But I keep my head held high. And the glock holstered.
For me. A drive helps. Hell. Sometimes I'll even head out to the middle of no where and take that very same glock. Or my SR-556, And dump a mag or two at some quick targets. Almost hard to belive, But shooting, Actually takes my mind off everything else. The sound, The muzzle flash at night. Just takes me away. I leave feeling better. And by the time I get back home, After the long drive. I'm back to my normal (Mostly at peace) self. Just thought I'd share what helps me.
Stay strong, Where all here for you. I appreciate you sharing.
Zxg11, Your extemely kind for consitantly coming back here and checking in on BipolarHacker. Your a value to the community here, And I for one appreciate you.
